groups.name: Quantum Physics and Information Technology (QPIT)
groups.quote: to understand, to engineer, and to control complex quantum systems of light and matter
groups.summary: A DTU Physics section that builds quantum systems of light and matter and uses them for computing, communication and sensing. Main lines are optical quantum computing with squeezed light and cluster states, continuous-variable quantum key distribution, quantum sensing with NV centres in diamond, and quantum optomechanics. The section is part of the bigQ centre (Center for Macroscopic Quantum States), the Copenhagen Center for Biomedical Quantum Sensing (CBQS) and Biomag.
themes: Optical quantum computing with squeezed light
centres: Copenhagen Center for Biomedical Quantum Sensing

groups.name: Quantum Information Science & Technology (NQCP)
groups.summary: The Niels Bohr Institute unit behind the Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP), with its own website at nqcp.ku.dk. Its members work across the stack of a future quantum computer: superconducting and hybrid superconductor–semiconductor qubits, spin qubits in semiconductor quantum dots, photonic qubits from colour centres in silicon, quantum algorithms for chemistry and open quantum systems, and strontium atomic clocks.
themes: Quantum algorithms for chemistry and open systems
centres: Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme

groups.name: Center for Complex Quantum Systems (CCQ)
groups.quote: advance our understanding of collective quantum phenomena in large collections of particles
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at Aarhus University, started in September 2020. It studies collective quantum behaviour in many atoms, ions and photons and builds hybrid systems where these meet: ion Coulomb crystals and ion traps (Drewsen), Bose–Einstein condensates and impurities (Arlt) and theory of polarons and many-body physics (Bruun). Former founding groups of Klaus Mølmer (now KU) and Thomas Pohl (now TU Wien) remain partners.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: Center for Polariton-driven Light-Matter Interactions (POLIMA)
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at SDU's Mads Clausen Institute. It studies how light couples to matter at the nanoscale through polaritons: quantum and nonlocal plasmonics in metals, polaritons in graphene and other 2D materials, excitons, free-electron–light interaction and cathodoluminescence. The work is mostly theory, with experiments in electron-beam spectroscopy and nanophotonics.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence

groups.name: Classique – Center for Classical Communication in the Quantum Era
teacher_units: Classique – Center for Classical Communication in the Quantum Era
Classical and Quantum Information and Connectivity
groups.quote: revolutionize communication systems for the quantum age
groups.summary: A Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence at Aalborg University (2025–2031). It asks how classical communication networks must change to serve both ordinary data and quantum information, which is fragile and time-limited. Researchers from communication engineering, physics, mathematics and computer science work on hybrid classical–quantum and satellite networks, physics-based models of quantum components, data compression and coding, and verification of quantum protocols.
centres: Danish National Research Foundation Center of Excellence
